noveltyJustification: Six findings are fully new (actions and boundaries, unit model, artifact table, battery pattern, route bindings, the detection gap); one consolidates the doctor surface and counts as half new.
ruledOut: Extending the release engine unit model to cover specs/

label: /doctor:update has five actions with explicit mutation classes: check (read-only), align (decisions in an ignored run dir), apply (preview, one startup approval, apply, verify), rollback (restore paths or clear a stale lock after approval), record-base (record the release base for a copied or fresh install).
The release engine is unit-based with kinds root, skill, command and directory, all under .skilled; there is no unit kind for specs/, so a user's spec corpus is outside the engine model.

Generated-artifact patterns (leaf manifests, skill graph-metadata derived blocks, trigger index and sidecars, compiled-route manifests) all live under .skilled/; spec-corpus description.json/graph-metadata.json are not in the table, so update cannot repair spec-derived metadata.

The post-apply battery is the ready-made integration pattern: each check is a name, when-condition, read-only command and documented repair (with approval, run the same command without --check), with engine rollback on failure.

The route manifest binds the trigger phrase spec-kit version migration to /doctor:update, so operators already reach for update to migrate an old tree, but the action set has no spec-corpus stage: a discoverability gap, not a missing engine.

/doctor:speckit is retrieval diagnostics only (trigger-index staleness, a lookup probe, the ripgrep recipe, citation-drift census), all read-only; its route entry shows the shape a new corpus route would follow.

Nothing in the doctor surface detects an old/pre-v4 repo as such: update compares against a recorded release base per tooling unit and speckit checks index staleness; corpus oldness is only visible by running the validator and classifying failures, which upgrade-legacy already does internally.

direction: Extending the release engine unit model to cover specs/
reason: The engine syncs release-owned files against a base; packet repairs are content-shaped work with refusal boundaries and a grandfathering record, so they belong in the pipeline.
Its routes are diagnostics and its contract keeps them read-only.
